question: Keshav invests a sum of ₹5400 and Tushar invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 3 years, Tushar gets ₹360 more interest than Keshav, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in principal amounts = ₹10200 − ₹5400 = ₹4800

Difference in simple interest for 3 years = ₹360

Difference in interest for 1 year = 360 ÷ 3 = ₹120

Rate of interest = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Difference in principal) × 100

Rate = (120 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5%.**

**Given:**

Keshav's principal (P₁) = ₹5400

Tushar's principal (P₂) = ₹10200

Time (T) = 3 years
